gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-bitter: Bitter has a very large lowercase and an s you can see right through, which makes paragraphs feel sturdy and unhurried. Bitter also lets the stencil-cut weight of Balsamiq Sans stand out as the loud one.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-instrument-sans: Loose, hand-built energy up top, then a tidy turn below: Balsamiq Sans has no pinched curves, while Instrument Sans keeps every stroke uniform. Its c opens like pincers.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-inter: Chunky and cheerful, then smooth as a tube. Balsamiq Sans is the one to make noise with, and Inter is the one that stays readable with its big counters and tall lowercase.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-mulish: Approachable from the first line, since Balsamiq Sans carries a stencil-cut weight with no tight, pinched curves. Mulish then keeps a long page easy on the eye, with open horseshoe apertures and no thick-and-thin modulation.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-poppins: Poppins reads with rope-loose curves and a tall, sturdy lowercase, never flickering between thick and thin strokes. And Balsamiq Sans, with its stencil-cut weight, gives the pair a bold, expressive streak.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-roboto-slab: Precise and structured, Roboto Slab fills the middle of each line, while Balsamiq Sans has horizontals and verticals as uniform as rod stock. That difference in lowercase height is the pair's hook.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-rubik: Soft and friendly, Rubik sets lowercase that looks big beside its capitals, with round shapes that stay clear. Balsamiq Sans adds lines that hold their thickness, so the heading looks bolder and more playful than the quieter body beneath it.
gen-gf-basic-fs-erode: Erode reads with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Yet Basic, with its high squared-off x-height, supplies the crisp sans-serif front, and the mix of styles is the real draw.
gen-gf-basic-fs-karma: Karma finishes its terminals well clear of the stem and keeps its modulation gentle enough never to snag the eye. And Basic, with its high squared-off x-height, gives that trustworthy serif body a crisp, modern sans-serif lead-in.
gen-gf-baumans-bitter: Baumans draws every stroke at one thickness, with a c like a wrench opened wide, and that is where it does its best work. Bitter handles the other job, with its big lowercase and open s keeping text dependable.
